retrieval_text: A 2-month-old male infant presented with a mass in the right lower limb, noted since birth and progressively enlarging. The mass measured approximately 5 × 5 cm, with a purplish-red discoloration and surrounding tissue swelling. The infant's past medical history, personal history, and immunization status were normal. There were no episodes of cyanosis, convulsions, or bleeding postnatally. Family history was negative for congenital malformations, tumors, or hemorrhagic conditions. On examination, the infant's vital signs were stable, and he was alert. Hemorrhagic spots were noted on the upper hard palate. A 5 × 5 cm mass was present at the right knee joint, which was warm to the touch, of medium consistency, and well-defined. No abnormalities were detected in the central nervous, cardiovascular, or respiratory systems.
A 54-year-old Caucasian male presented with abdominal pain and bloating, for which he had been using nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).

A 59-year-old, right-handed female with 12 years of education presented with a 2-year history of difficulty understanding spoken language. She had a background of well-controlled hypertension for 5 years. The patient reported that spoken conversation sounded like noise or buzzing, especially in crowded areas. She could not understand spoken questions during the interview but could comprehend and respond correctly through lip reading or gestural cues. She struggled to understand television dialogue but could follow foreign movies with Korean subtitles without issue. Environmental noises like doorbells and ringing phones were perceived and responded to appropriately. Her family noted no issues with her ability to express thoughts, recall events, navigate directions, or use public transportation. She managed household tasks, financial matters, and social activities without difficulty. A hearing aid prescribed by an otolaryngology clinic did not improve her comprehension. One year after symptom onset, she began making errors in simple mathematics and her spoken language comprehension declined significantly, though she could still read and write. Her writing style became rough with frequent spelling errors. She occasionally forgot things but it did not impact daily life. She had trouble recalling names of familiar neighbors but recognized them visually. Her demeanor and personal relationships remained unaffected.

A 53-year-old male presented with multiple, dusky reddish nodules on the trunk, persisting for 7 years. These lesions were bilaterally distributed along the lateral sides of the trunk and had shown slight progression. The patient has a medical history of arterial hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. There were no systemic symptoms indicating involvement of other organs. The patient did not report any specific triggers causing induction or exacerbation of symptoms. Stroking the lesions resulted in swelling, itching, and redness of the skin.

A 43-year-old man visited the outpatient endocrine clinic at Tabriz University of Medical Sciences, Tabriz, Iran, accompanied by his sister, for an assessment of skin lesions. The patient exhibited multiple lesions on his shoulders, back, the lateral and medial parts of the dorsal surface of his feet, the medial and lateral malleus of both feet, and the dorsal and palmar surfaces of both hands. His siblings have been monitored in the same clinic for similar skin conditions. These conditions were characterized by palmar, eruptive, tuberous, and trauma site xanthomas, along with elevated levels of both total cholesterol and triglycerides in the plasma. Both parents had normal serum lipid levels. There was no history of coronary artery or other atherosclerotic disorders in the patient or his siblings. The patient reported no other complaints and maintained an active lifestyle as a greengrocer.
A 19-year-old female presented to the emergency room with left-sided chest pain and cough.

A 10-year-old female from a rural area in Kendrapada district, Odisha, presented to the pediatrics outpatient department with intermittent abdominal pain, anal itching, and restlessness at night for the past 2-3 weeks. Physical examination revealed no notable findings.

An 80-year-old woman presented with difficulty in raising her right upper limb, progressive dyskinesia, and gait disorder. She had experienced neck pain for approximately 2 years and numbness in her extremities for about a year, both of which had worsened significantly before her visit. She could walk unassisted for less than 100 meters. Muscle weakness (manual muscle testing [MMT] score: 3) was observed in the entire right upper limb, while strength in the remaining limbs was normal. Hypesthesia was noted throughout the upper and lower limbs. Deep tendon reflexes were increased bilaterally in all limbs, with positive Hoffman’s and Wartenberg’s signs.

On March 7, 2018, a 35-year-old Chinese female presented with a one-year history of persistent erythematous papules and infiltrative plaques on the nose without any obvious triggers. Initially, a hard nodule the size of rice grains appeared on the right alar part of the nose, which was painless and itchy. Over time, the skin lesions gradually increased in size, became thick, and spread across the entire nose. Infiltrating plaques also developed on the upper jaw. Past and family history revealed no similar diseases within the family. Since the onset of the illness, the patient’s urine, stool, and weight remained normal. Skin examination revealed diffuse erythematous papules, infiltrations, and hypertrophic plaques on the entire nose and upper jaw, with a smooth surface.
A 32-year-old woman reported experiencing painless unilateral blurring of vision in her left eye for the past three months.

A 14-year-old male, weighing 45 kg, was transferred to our clinic for further evaluation after being found to have pericardial effusion at a provincial hospital. Initial symptoms included fever and left shoulder pain. Physical examination revealed a reduction in the intensity of cardiac sounds and an elevated heart rate. Notably, the patient did not exhibit arthralgia or abdominal pain at any point during the clinical course.

A 5-day-old male neonate presented with widespread jaundice. He was born at term via vaginal delivery, weighing approximately 2100 g. The mother, with a history of six pregnancies and six live births, was generally healthy except for mild photosensitivity. The neonate had no history of clay-colored stools, fever, or drug administration. On admission, physical examination showed pale conjunctiva, yellowing of the sclera, generalized jaundice, a few red lesions around the eyes, and mild enlargement of the spleen. The pulse was irregular, with a heart rate of about 75 beats per minute.

A one-day-old male infant, born at term with a birth weight of 3.1 kg, presented with no significant prenatal history and an uncomplicated delivery. Since birth, the infant had not passed stool and exhibited increased bilious vomiting and abdominal swelling. The anus was observed to be in a normal position with well-developed gluteal muscles and skin folds. The genital examination showed normally developed male genitalia with no visible signs of a fistula. The urine was clear and free from meconium contamination. A catheter could not be inserted more than half an inch into the anal opening.

A 32-year-old adequately nourished male was admitted with complaints of shortness of breath for 1 month, which had worsened over the past 2 days. He had no other accompanying symptoms. The patient, who worked as a tailor and consumed a mixed diet, was found to be well-built and nourished with a body mass index of 25.3 kg/m2. On examination, he was tachypneic, had tachycardia, and a mild fever. Oral thrush was observed, and scrapings were sent for fungal culture. There were no apparent risk factors for immunosuppressive states.
A 17-year-old female presented with a 7-month history of intermittent swelling in the lower extremities, protein in the urine, and blood in the urine.

A 26-year-old male visited Tianjin Medical University General Hospital due to a painless neck lump, first noticed 6 years ago, which had recently grown rapidly. The patient experienced agitation, irritability, excessive sweating, and discomfort while swallowing.

A 49-year-old male was admitted in July 2010 due to sudden onset of weakness in the proximal muscles of his limbs, affecting both sensory and motor functions. Upon clinical examination, he exhibited muscle weakness in the proximal regions of both upper and lower limbs, accompanied by sensations of tingling and pain. The muscle stretch reflexes in his lower limbs were reduced. There were no signs of upper motor neuron involvement.

An 8-year-old girl from a rural area presented with pain in her left leg and an ulcer on the anterior aspect of her left shin, persisting for 15 days. These symptoms have been recurring over the past 4 years. The ulcer typically healed with antibiotics but reappeared after a few days.

A 72-year-old woman experienced behavioural changes, unsteadiness, and frequent falls over the past year. She had started oral anticoagulant therapy two years earlier due to paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. Relatives reported that over the past year, she became more listless and neglected work and domestic activities. She also exhibited hyperreligious behaviour, anxiety, loss of appetite, mild lower limb weakness, and falls. Subsequently, she experienced periods of agitation, confusion, and visual hallucinations, leading to the initiation of antipsychotic medication. Her condition worsened, resulting in the loss of her ability to walk and confinement to a wheelchair.

A 21-month-old male presented to the emergency department with respiratory symptoms. Over the past 10 months, there has been a noted increase in penile size and skin darkening. A sibling passed away 13 years ago with similar symptoms. The patient's weight was 13 kg (Z-score: 1.1, 85.3th percentile), height was 92 cm (Z-score: 2.4, 99.2th percentile), and blood pressure was 139/90 mmHg (Z-score for age-based pediatric blood pressure for systolic/diastolic pressure: 4.3/3.9, 100th percentile. Z-score equal to or greater than 95th percentile indicates hypertension). Physical examination revealed hyperpigmentation of the gums, skin, and scrotum, facial acne, and penile enlargement measuring 8.7 cm (above 90th percentile). Testicular size was prepubertal (less than 2 mL) with no pubic hair.
